entries.title: Fundamental principles of public buying
entries.text: Every authority buying goods for public service is responsible and accountable for bringing efficiency, economy and transparency to the purchase, for fair and equitable treatment of suppliers, and for promoting competition.

entries.title: Standards of financial propriety
entries.text: An officer should spend public money with the same care a person of ordinary prudence would spend their own. Expenditure should not be more than the occasion demands, and no authority should sanction expenditure that benefits itself.

entries.title: Buy through GeM when the item is listed
entries.text: Procurement of goods and services that are available on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is to be made through GeM. Check GeM first; the buying mode on GeM depends on the value of the purchase and the GeM rules in force.

entries.title: Purchase without quotation
entries.text: Goods up to ₹2,00,000 on each occasion may be bought without inviting quotations, on the basis of a certificate by the competent authority that the goods are of the requisite quality and specification and were bought from a reliable supplier at a reasonable price.

entries.title: Purchase by a local purchase committee
entries.text: Goods costing above ₹2,00,000 and up to ₹25,00,000 on each occasion may be bought on the recommendation of a duly constituted purchase committee of three members. The committee surveys the market to establish a reasonable price, quality and specification, identifies a suitable supplier, and records a joint certificate.

entries.title: Limited Tender Enquiry
entries.text: Limited Tender Enquiry may be adopted when the estimated value of the goods is up to ₹1 crore. Bids are invited from registered or known suppliers; GeM-registered suppliers are prima facie eligible.

entries.title: Advertised (open) Tender Enquiry
entries.text: Procurement of goods with an estimated value above ₹1 crore is to be made through an advertised tender enquiry, published on the Central Public Procurement Portal and run through e-procurement.

entries.title: Single tender and proprietary items
entries.text: Single tender enquiry may be adopted when only one firm makes the required goods (a proprietary item), in a defined emergency, or for standardisation with existing equipment. A proprietary article certificate must be recorded, and the reason documented.

entries.title: Do not split a demand
entries.text: A demand should not be divided into smaller quantities to make piecemeal purchases for the purpose of avoiding the sanction of a higher authority. Related requirements are combined and judged at their total value.

entries.ref: Ch. 3, expenditure control (rule number to verify)
entries.title: Avoid the March rush
entries.text: A rush of expenditure in the closing months of the financial year is treated as a breach of financial propriety. Cash management instructions cap the share of the year's budget that may be spent in the last quarter and in March.

entries.ref: Ch. 3, savings and surrender (rule number to verify)
entries.title: Surrender savings in time
entries.text: Savings that cannot be used should be surrendered as soon as they are foreseen, and before the financial year closes, so the money can be used elsewhere. Funds not spent by 31 March lapse and do not carry forward.

entries.title: Which manual applies to your case
entries.text: DPM 2025 governs revenue procurement by the Services from 1 November 2025, replacing DPM 2009. Cases where the RFP was issued on or before 31 October 2025 continue under DPM 2009 as amended; RFPs issued or reissued on or after 1 November 2025 follow DPM 2025. Capital acquisition is outside the DPM.

entries.title: The steps of a revenue purchase
entries.text: A revenue purchase runs: statement of case with necessity, choice of procurement mode by value, enquiry or RFP, receipt and opening of bids, evaluation and comparative statement, sanction of the competent financial authority, supply order, receipt and inspection, taking on charge, and the bill to the paying authority.

entries.title: Tender Purchase Committee
entries.text: For tendered purchases a Tender Purchase Committee examines the bids, prepares the comparative statement and recommends the supplier to the competent financial authority. Its composition depends on the value of the case and the level of the sanctioning authority.

entries.title: Contract Negotiation Committee
entries.text: Where only one vendor is in the running, such as a proprietary or single tender case, a Contract Negotiation Committee negotiates the price before sanction and records why the price is reasonable.

entries.ref: Vol I, receipt and inspection (summary, verify)
entries.title: Receipt, inspection and taking on charge
entries.text: Stores are received and inspected against the supply order, normally by a board of officers, then taken on charge in the unit ledger. The inspection note and receipt voucher go with the bill.

entries.title: What DFPDS is and which version applies
entries.text: DFPDS sets, schedule by schedule, which authority may sanction how much for which item, and whether the power is used with or without IFA concurrence. DFPDS 2021 introduced emergency financial powers for field formations below Command level. A revised delegation is reported to have been released in June 2026; confirm which version your formation is applying.

entries.title: Who sanctions how much
entries.text: Sanction is given by the lowest authority whose delegated ceiling for that schedule item covers the full value of the case. Sample ceilings used in this POC: Commanding Officer up to ₹5 lakh, Brigade Commander up to ₹25 lakh, GOC Division up to ₹1 crore, GOC Corps up to ₹3 crore, GOC-in-C up to ₹10 crore, beyond that Army HQ or MoD. These are placeholders, not DFPDS figures.

entries.title: When IFA concurrence is needed
entries.text: Each DFPDS schedule says whether a power is exercised with or without the concurrence of the Integrated Financial Adviser. This POC uses a single placeholder: concurrence above ₹10 lakh. A sanction given without required concurrence is not valid.

entries.title: Is the item authorised to the unit?
entries.text: Whether a unit may hold an item comes from its equipment tables and authorised scales, not from GFR, DFPDS or DPM. Items not on the scales need a separate special sanction before any purchase is planned.

entries.title: Centrally supplied or bought locally?
entries.text: Many items reach units through central provisioning: the unit raises a demand on the depot rather than buying. Local purchase is for items that are locally procurable, or for urgent needs where the depot cannot supply, and usually needs a non-availability certificate.

entries.title: Budget heads
entries.text: Funds reach the unit under budget heads, and every purchase is booked to one. The same item can only be bought from the head it belongs to; money under one head cannot simply be used for another without re-appropriation by the authority that allotted it.

entries.title: Allotment, commitment and expenditure
entries.text: Allotment is what you were given under a head. Commitment is what you have promised through orders that are not yet paid. Expenditure is what the accounts office has booked. What you can still spend is allotment minus commitment minus expenditure, not allotment minus payments.

entries.title: Bills and the paying office
entries.text: Bills go to the Controller of Defence Accounts, who checks them before paying. A bill is objected to when the sanction, supply order, receipt or inspection papers are missing or do not agree. Attach the full set the first time.

entries.title: Is it public money at all?
entries.text: Officers' and JCOs' messes, clubs and unit institutes usually furnish and equip themselves from their own regimental (non-public) funds, which run under their own rules rather than GFR. Before planning a purchase, settle which fund the item belongs to: an office, barrack, cookhouse or training area is public money; a mess, club or institute usually is not.

entries.title: What this tool does not cover
entries.text: This tool covers revenue purchases from public funds. It does not cover capital acquisition, regimental or other non-public funds, pay and allowances, or works executed by the engineer services.
